conclusion: Snapshot GET paging avoids SQL re-execution, but UI integration, idempotent creation, S3 page indexing, and wide-row chunk sizing remain before a high-concurrency rollout.

fixed.issue: Unbounded snapshot creation can consume shared HTTP workers, database connections and staging disk.
fixed.change: Async admission before thread dispatch; EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT_CREATES=4 per worker, 429 EXPORT_BUSY with Retry-After for excess requests. Per-worker only, not distributed.

fixed.issue: Concurrent cold lru_cache misses can construct multiple Couchbase/S3 clients.
fixed.change: Serialize store resolution around cached initialization.

fixed.issue: Each S3 upload can spawn a nested transfer pool and metadata body reads did not explicitly close responses.
fixed.change: Disable transfer threads per upload; close metadata response bodies explicitly.

open.issue: UI still executes SQL on every /query/page request.
open.required_change: Create/retain one snapshot ID per answer table/version, use snapshot GET pages for scrolling. Avoid issuing both old query/page and snapshot calls.

open.issue: Duplicate POSTs/retries create separate UUIDs and execute SQL repeatedly. No idempotency key or distributed single-flight.
open.required_change: Store-backed atomic idempotency claim scoped to caller and request fingerprint; handle in-progress and completed retries. Admission control is not deduplication.

open.issue: Each S3 page rescans gzip JSONL from row zero. Deep pages do O(offset) decode/read work per request.
open.required_change: Chunk/index S3 row objects; keep CSV parts as separate download artifacts.

open.issue: Couchbase chunks are bounded by row count only; wide chunks can exceed document-size limits and cause large decoding allocations on concurrent reads. CSV part byte cap also permits an oversized single row.
open.required_change: Enforce byte bounds and page through chunk offsets recorded in metadata; reject a single oversized record explicitly.

open.issue: Abort cleanup calls finish(), which can flush pending Couchbase rows or retry a failed chunk write during exception unwinding.
open.required_change: Separate successful finalization from abort close/discard; preserve the original failure.

live_couchbase_concurrency.note: Zero additional query connections was asserted immediately after paging, before the separate creation burst.

s3_algorithm_probe.storage: in-memory S3 adapter with actual gzip paging algorithm

regression: 203 passed (snapshot, auth, session and diagnostic tests after concurrency fixes)
limitations: Concurrency test used local synthetic 24-row snapshots; not a production-capacity benchmark.
Couchbase pages tested with 16 workers and mixed caller identities; create burst exercised live Trino.
S3 deep-page probe used in-memory storage with the real gzip paging algorithm, not a network throughput benchmark.
No agent/UI implementation changes in this review.
